title: Orthogonality implies local principal completeness
statement: On a small site (C,J), let A be a commutative Noetherian ring and n a natural number whose image in A is a nonzerodivisor. For an arbitrary unbounded derived sheaf of modules M over the constant ring sheaf A, orthogonality to every V on which multiplication by n is invertible implies local derived completeness for the kernel of constant A → constant A/(n), in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The derived categories are the specified standard localizations.

source.place: Stacks Tags 091Q and 0999; principal localization and local derived completeness

proof.text: Use the kernel sections formula and the constant quotient kernel description in flat_and_quotients at exponent zero. Every constant element of (n) is divisible by n after constant sheafification, which preserves natural casts and multiplication. Ideal.span_le therefore puts every section of the kernel in the sectionwise principal ideal (n). Extract a factorization f = n*a.

On the slice over U, restrict f = n*a along every structural arrow. In the actual sectionwise localization at f, the product of the images of n and a is a unit, hence the image of n is a unit. Multiplication by n is bijective on every localization ring, hence an isomorphism of underlying additive presheaves and of module presheaves. Additive module sheafification and the additive degree-zero derived functor preserve this isomorphism.

The exact left adjoint of restriction to the slice exists by localized_restriction_extension_exists. Extend its adjunction degreewise to complexes and descend both exact functors through their standard quasi-isomorphism localizations. Additivity carries n-invertible objects on the slice to n-invertible global objects, so the derived adjunction transports global orthogonality to the restricted target.

On a small ringed site, take the existing native symmetric derived tensor and its adjunction to the recorded derived internal Hom. Tensor functors are additive because they are left adjoints; symmetry gives additivity in the parameter. If L is n-invertible, then H tensor L is n-invertible for H = RHom(L,M). Orthogonality and tensor-Hom adjunction make End(H) a subsingleton. Thus its identity is zero and H is zero. Apply this on every slice with its localization at f, yielding exactly IsLocallyDerivedRingedIdealComplete for the kernel ideal.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08J9 (derived tensor-Hom), together with sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ (exact slice extension), algebraization.tex Tag 0999 and more-algebra.tex Tag 091Q. G7 uses the endomorphism test instead of a family of shifted generators.

lean.statement:
theorem constantPrincipalComplete_of_orthogonal
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (n : ℕ)
    (hn : (n : A) ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (M : D (constant J A))
    (hM : ∀ V : D (constant J A), IsIso (n • 𝟙 V) → Subsingleton (V ⟶ M)) :
    IsComplete (quotient J A (Ideal.span {(n : A)}) 0) M
